opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. As full-time employee, maximum is write (admin only for role-owned systems, and Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist). Requested level (write) equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Eric Woods (E019) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read unless they have advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds the max, so recommend read.
reason: HR's authoritative record (Note 1) shows Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time employee (looked up in the HR database) with role Engineer, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Per policy, a full-time employee's maximum is write (admin only for role-owned systems). The requested level (write) equals the maximum, so write is granted. Note 2's contractor classification comes from the Security database, but employment type is an HR-authoritative fact; even so, both notes agree on role, and granting write remains within policy for a full-time employee.
